  Fetch the records in a window of days around each person's entry: the 30 days
  after discharge, and the year before admission.
---

knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Print results at most 60 characters wide, "#> " included, to fit a printed page.
options(width = 57)
# Keep the build machine out of printed query headers (load duckdb first, as it
# registers its own description when it loads).
loadNamespace("duckdb")
registerS3method("db_connection_describe", "duckdb_connection",
                 function(con, ...) "example database", envir = asNamespace("dbplyr"))

In [From question to cohort](question-to-cohort.html) you built `entries`: one
row per person, with the dates of their first admission for appendicitis. To
answer the running question, you now need two more sets of records for each
person:

- **Follow-up:** admissions for any cause in the 30 days after discharge, to
  find readmissions.
- **Look-back:** admissions in the year before the entry admission, where, with
  the entry admission itself, the next guide looks for diabetes.

Each person has their own dates, so each needs their own window. The picture
shows three people. Their windows sit at different dates, and a record comes
back only if it falls inside one of its own person's windows.

```{r windows-timeline, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# Inline, so the diagram travels with the page and keeps its title and description.
cat("```{=html}", "<div style=\"margin: 0.5rem 0 1.5rem;\">",
    readLines("figures/windows-timeline.svg"), "</div>", "```", sep = "\n")
```

You fetch each kind of window with its own `thip_window()` call: follow-up
records into `followup`, look-back records into `history`.

Every example runs on the example database of invented records described in
[Meet the THIP data](meet-the-data.html); on THIP, connect with `thip_connect()`
instead.

## Rebuild the entries

This chunk repeats the recipe of [From question to cohort](question-to-cohort.html).

```{r rebuild}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

con <- thip_connect_example()

admissions <- thip_table(
  con,
  tables = c("nhso2565", "nhso2566", "nhso2567"),
  .id = "source_table",
  dates = c(adm = "dateadm", dsc = "datedsc"),
  date_format = c(adm = "%Y%m%d", dsc = "%Y%m%d")
)

candidates <- admissions |>
  filter(adm >= as.Date("2021-10-01"),
         adm <= as.Date("2024-08-31")) |>
  thip_filter_icd(codes = "K35", cols = "pdx",
                  match = "prefix") |>
  collect()

entries <- candidates |>
  filter(!is.na(dsc)) |>
  arrange(pid, adm, tran_id) |>
  distinct(pid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(pid, entry_id = tran_id,
         adm_date = adm, dsc_date = dsc)
```

There are `r nrow(entries)` entries, one per person. `adm_date` and `dsc_date`
are `Date` values, which the windows below need.

## The round trip

`entries` is in R and the records are on the database, so you cannot join the
two the usual way ([Working with a database from
R](database-from-r.html#join-tables-on-the-same-connection)). Getting each
person's records around their entry is a round trip:

1. `thip_window()` takes `entries` and makes a plan: for each entry, its `pid`
   and the first and last day of its window. Nothing is read yet.
2. `collect()` sends the plan to the database as a query. The database matches
   records to people by `pid`, checks each record's date against that person's
   window, and keeps only the records inside.
3. Those records come back to R as an ordinary data frame, with one extra
   column, `entry_id`, saying which entry each record belongs to.

## A window is two day offsets

A window is set by a date on the entry, the index date (see [From question to
cohort](question-to-cohort.html)), and two whole numbers of days counted from
it, smallest first (the `L` marks a whole number in R; `c(1, 31)` works too).
Negative offsets count back before the index date. For readmission, the index
date is the discharge date:

- `window = c(1L, 31L)` sets the edges: day 1 and day 31 after discharge.
- `bounds = "[)"`, the default, says which edges count. `[` includes its edge
  and `)` excludes it.

So the follow-up window holds days 1 to 30 after discharge. A record admitted on
the day of discharge (day 0) is not in it, and nor is one admitted on day 31.
As long as an admission does not start after its own discharge, the entry
admission cannot be in its own follow-up window; you check this below.

The other three bounds move the edges:

| `bounds`         | `window = c(1L, 31L)` includes |
|------------------|--------------------------------|
| `"[)"` (default) | days 1 to 30                   |
| `"[]"`           | days 1 to 31                   |
| `"(]"`           | days 2 to 31                   |
| `"()"`           | days 2 to 30                   |

Offsets count days, not calendar months or years: `c(1L, 31L)` is always the
same 30 days, whatever the month.

Try other windows in the explorer below: set the edges to `-365` and `0` for the
year before the index date, or switch the bounds and watch days 1 and 31.

```{r window-explorer, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# Inline, so the explorer travels with the page. file.path() keeps pkgdown from
# also copying the .html file to the site as a page of its own.
cat("```{=html}", readLines(file.path("figures", "window-explorer.html")), "```",
    sep = "\n")
```

## Plan the follow-up

The piped-in table is the records to search, `admissions`, trimmed to the
columns you need; `entries` is the second argument. `date = "adm"` names a
column of the records, the admission date, and `index = "dsc_date"` names a
column of `entries`:

```{r followup-plan}
followup_plan <- admissions |>
  select(pid, tran_id, source_table, adm, dsc, pdx) |>
  thip_window(entries, date = "adm", index = "dsc_date",
              window = c(1L, 31L))

followup_plan
```

Printing the plan reads no records: it describes `r nrow(entries)` entries for
`r nrow(entries)` people, waiting for `collect()`. In the printout, *source*
means the records you search (`admissions`) and *cohort* means `entries`. Do any
`select()` and `filter()` before `thip_window()`, as here; the plan is not a
table you can add more dplyr steps to.

Two arguments keep their defaults: `by = "pid"` names the person column, and
`entry = "entry_id"` the column that identifies each entry, one value per row.
Both dates must be `Date` values, not text, which is why the plan uses `adm`,
not `dateadm`. A missing value in `entries` stops `thip_window()` with an error,
one reason `entries` keeps only admissions with a discharge date; a record whose
date is missing, such as one that failed to convert, is never inside any window.
The [reference page](../reference/thip_window.html) has the details.

## Collect the follow-up

`collect()` runs the plan and brings the matching records into R:

```{r followup}
followup <- collect(followup_plan)
glimpse(followup)
```

`followup` has the six selected columns plus `entry_id`, the last column, which
names the entry each record belongs to. The entries' own dates are not in it. To
check the window, join each entry's discharge date back, count the days from
discharge to each readmission, and check that no entry admission came back as
its own readmission:

```{r followup-days}
followup |>
  left_join(select(entries, entry_id, dsc_date),
            by = "entry_id") |>
  mutate(days_after = as.integer(adm - dsc_date)) |>
  count(days_after)

followup |>
  filter(tran_id == entry_id) |>
  nrow()
```

Every readmission starts between day 1 and day 30 after discharge, and none is
the entry admission itself.

## Count readmissions per entry

`followup` has rows only for entries that were readmitted. Person B in the
picture at the top was not: it is in `entries` but has no rows in `followup`.
Each row will count as one readmission, so first check for repeated records, the
same record twice for one entry, which would count twice:

```{r repeats}
followup |>
  count(entry_id, tran_id) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  nrow()
```

There are none. If you find some, decide whether they are the same admission
before you count; `distinct(entry_id, tran_id, .keep_all = TRUE)` keeps the
first row of each, with all its columns.

To count every entry, including those with no readmission, start from `entries`
and join the counts onto it:

```{r readmit}
readmit <- entries |>
  left_join(
    count(followup, entry_id, name = "readmissions"),
    by = "entry_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(readmissions = coalesce(readmissions, 0L),
         readmitted = readmissions > 0)

readmit |>
  summarise(entries = n(), readmitted = sum(readmitted)) |>
  mutate(percent = round(100 * readmitted / entries, 1))
```

`r sum(readmit$readmitted)` of the `r nrow(readmit)` entries were readmitted,
for any cause, within 30 days of discharge. To count only related readmissions,
filter `followup` on `pdx` first.

**Keep `entries` on the left.** Counting from `followup` alone, or with
`inner_join()`, drops the `r sum(!readmit$readmitted)` entries with no
readmission, and every entry left looks readmitted.

## Look back a year

The same function fetches the look-back records. Now the index date is the
admission date, and the window ends at it:

```{r history}
history <- admissions |>
  select(pid, tran_id, source_table, adm, dsc, pdx,
         num_range("sdx", 1:20)) |>
  thip_window(entries, date = "adm", index = "adm_date",
              window = c(-365L, 0L)) |>
  collect()
```

With `"[)"`, the window holds days −365 to −1: the 365 days before the entry
admission. The entry admission starts on day 0, so it is not in `history`; its
diagnoses are already in `candidates`. `history` keeps the principal diagnosis
and all 20 secondary diagnosis columns, which the next guide searches, plus
`entry_id`.

`history` holds `r nrow(history)` records, for
`r n_distinct(history$entry_id)` of the `r nrow(entries)` entries; for the
others no admission was found in the year before, which is not the same as
having no diabetes and, as the next section shows, does not always mean that a
whole year was searched.

## Windows and the years you stacked

A window searches every table stacked in `admissions`, across fiscal years, but
nothing outside them. To check that the windows fit, take the first and last
admission dates in the stack from the data, not from the tables' names, and
count the windows that run past them:

```{r coverage}
span <- admissions |>
  summarise(first = min(adm, na.rm = TRUE),
            last = max(adm, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  collect()
span

coverage <- entries |>
  summarise(
    lookback_early = sum(adm_date - 365L < span$first),
    followup_late = sum(dsc_date + 30L > span$last)
  )
coverage
```

No follow-up window runs past the last admission date: the study period stops a
month before the data end to leave room for follow-up. The look-back has no
such room at the start: for the `r coverage$lookback_early` entries
admitted in fiscal year 2565, part of the year before lies before the first
stacked table, so finding no history there can mean the records are in a table
you did not stack.

There are two fixes. Stack the previous year's table as well (on THIP, add it
to `tables` and run this check again), keeping the study period as it is; or
start the study period a year after the data begin, on 1 October 2022 here. The
example has no earlier table, so this course keeps all `r nrow(entries)`
entries, and the next guide reads a missing diabetes code as "not recorded in
the stacked years".

## Explicit start and end dates

Instead of `index` and `window`, you can give each entry its own first and last
day as two `Date` columns, named with `start` and `end`; here is the same
follow-up written as dates, with `"[]"` so that both days count:

```{r explicit}
followup_again <- admissions |>
  select(pid, tran_id, source_table, adm, dsc, pdx) |>
  thip_window(
    mutate(entries, fu_start = dsc_date + 1L,
           fu_end = dsc_date + 30L),
    date = "adm", start = "fu_start", end = "fu_end",
    bounds = "[]"
  ) |>
  collect()

setequal(followup_again$tran_id, followup$tran_id)
```

The same records come back; dates suit a window that is not a fixed number of
days from one date, such as from discharge to the end of the study.

## Batches and the window report

`collect()` sends people to the database in batches of at most `batch_size`
people, 1,000 by default. All of one person's windows go in the same batch and
every matching record comes back, so smaller batches mean more, shorter queries
and the same result. Every collected result carries a report of its run:

```{r batches}
followup_small <- collect(followup_plan, batch_size = 100L)
attr(followup_small, "window_report")
```

Here `r nrow(attr(followup_small, "window_report")$batches)` batches bring back
the same `r nrow(followup_small)` records as one batch. `matched_entries` and
`unmatched_entries` count the entries with and without records, here the
`r sum(readmit$readmitted)` readmitted and the `r sum(!readmit$readmitted)`
others, and `batches` shows each batch's people, entries and matching records.
`complete` is always `TRUE` on a result you get back, because a failed batch
stops with an error instead of returning part of the result. If a batch's query
grows too large, `collect()` stops and asks for a smaller `batch_size`; every
returned record still ends up in R's memory, so select the columns you need
before you plan.

## Several entries per person

Here each person has one entry. If you keep several entries per person, as in
[Every admission as an
entry](question-to-cohort.html#every-admission-as-an-entry), each needs its own
`entry_id`. Their windows may then overlap, and a record inside two windows
comes back twice, once for each
entry. That is right when you count per entry. To count a person's admissions
instead, keep one of each with `distinct(pid, tran_id)`.

## In short

- `thip_window()` plans a round trip: each entry's person and window go to the
  database, and `collect()` brings back only the records inside, labelled with
  `entry_id`.
- A window is an index date and two day offsets, or two dates with `start` and
  `end`. With the default bounds, `"[)"`, `c(1L, 31L)` from discharge is days 1
  to 30, and `c(-365L, 0L)` from admission is the year before it, without the
  entry admission.
- A window searches only the tables you stacked: check that every window fits
  inside them.
- Entries with no records are not in the result: start from `entries` and
  left-join.
- `thip_window()` keeps every match, so check for repeated records within an
  entry before you count.
- `batch_size` counts people, not rows, and does not change the result;
  `attr(x, "window_report")` summarises the run.
